full_judgment:
"Let a Rule be issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the orders No. 144, 148,149, 150, 151, 153, 154, 156, 158, 160 & 163 dated 4-4-2017 as well as the order dated 138 dated 24-5-2017 passed by the Special Judge, Court No. 03, Dhaka in Special Cases No. 12-26 of 2007 rejecting the he application for holding one trial of the accused petitioners under section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 should not be set aside and also why the opposite parties should not be directed to allow the accused petitioners to be tried in one trial in respect of Special Case No. 12-26 of 2007, now pending n the Court of Special Judge, Court No. 3, Dhaka, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 3. The prosecution story in all the cases are that on 29-3-2007 one Md Shafiul Alam, Assistant Director of Anti Corruption Commission ACC, Dhaka lodged an ejahar with Motijheel Police Station. Dhaka against the accused petitioners under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code along with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 alleging misappropriation of government money amounting of Taka 127,64,19,059.26  by way of misuse of power and in collusion with each other sold 18 abandoned buildings through tender process to the buyers showing less value than actual value and hence misappropriated the said amount and, as such, committed criminal offence. The accused petitioners are concerned minister and others are members of value evaluation committee of RAJUK and hence the case. 

 6. Thereafter, the accused petitioners filed an application for holding one trial of the accused petitioners under section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 before the trial Court and upon hearing of the said application on 4-4-2017 the Court below was pleased to reject the said application vide order dated 4-4-2017. Against the said order the petitioners obtained rule and order of stay. 

 7. Mr Rokan Uddin Mahmood. the learned advocate appearing along with Mr MA Hannan, the learned advocate for the petitioners submitted that the trial Court without considering the materials on record and not applying the judicial mind most illegally rejected the application filed by the accused petitioners under section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958, in a mechanical way which is liable to be set aside to secure ends of justice. He also submitted that the petitioners being the common accused's in Special Cases No. 12-26 of 2007, now pending before the Court of Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka arising out of one First Information Report i.e. Motijheel Case No. 140(3)2007 filed by ACC against 12 accused’s for causing financial loss of Taka 127,64,19,049.26 under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code red with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and, as such, the provision of section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is attracted and shall be tried at one trial for all such offences as levelled against them in all the 15 cases for ends of justice and the trial Court has committed error of law in not allowing the said applications. 

 9. Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties No. 1 and 2-ACC by filing a counter affidavit stated that against the ad-interim order of stay passed by the High Court Division the opposite party No. 2-ACC preferred Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division being Criminal Petition No. 599 of 2017. On 13-7-2017 the Appellate Division disposed the Criminal Petition with a direction to the High Court Division to dispose of the Rule within 6 (six) weeks by the Rules issuing Bench. He submitted that in the instant case the argument advanced on behalf of the accused petitioners with regard to section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 which has no manner of application in the case, because the period of one year is available in section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, but it is absent in section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and thereby in view of the provision laid down in section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 section 6(1B) excludes the application of section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which relates to the period of the commission of the alleged offence and, as such, the question of applicability of section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 has no manner of application. He also submitted that in the case of State vs Md Ibrahim Ali reported in 66 DLR (AD) 33 it has been held that any number of offences punishable under the Criminal Law Amendment Act, irrespective of the period over which the offence was committed, may be tried at one trial. All the offences committed over any length of period of time could be tried in one trial upon framing one charge. But the said case is not applicable in the instant case, because the offence is distinct and independent in view of the different houses mentioned in the 15 charge sheets and, as such, question of application of section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 does not arise. Finally, he submitted that the accused petitioners filed one after another application only to frustrate the trial and in view of the repeated directions by the Superior Court the accused petitioners interrupted the trial by filing frivolous applications. 

 10. We have gone through the application, the First Information Report (FIR) and the charge sheet as well as the other materials available in the record. We have also considered the submissions of the learned advocates for both the sides. In the instant case, only one question of law is to be decided, whether the provision of section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 is applicable in this case. Sections 6(1) and 6(1B) runs as follows: 

 Thus, the argument advanced on behalf of the accused petitioners with regard to section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 which has no manner of application, because from a scrutiny it appears that the period of one year is available in section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, but it is absent in section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 and thereby in view of the provision laid down in section 6(1) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act. 1958 section 6(1B) excludes the application of section 234 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which relates to the period of the commission of the alleged offence. Furthermore, the offence is distinct and independent in view of the different houses mentioned in 15 charge sheets and, as such, question of applicability of section 6(1B) of the Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958 has no manner of application.
